correction.text: Cliopatria's 1932 shape (Canada without Newfoundland and Labrador) applied back to 1880

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: on 1 September 1880 'The United Kingdom transferred its Arctic Islands to Canada'. Everything later until 1949 is internal (Yukon 13 June 1898, Alberta and Saskatchewan 1 September 1905, Ontario, Quebec and Manitoba extended north on 15 May 1912) or sea (the NWT's maritime boundary extended to the Pole on 1 June 1925); the Alaska boundary was fixed on 20 October 1903 and the Labrador boundary decided in 1927 in Newfoundland's favour, so Labrador stays outside until 1949.

9.63 M km2 for 1932-1948. Infobox total 9,984,670 km2 (11.76% water, 2015); this shape plus Newfoundland and Labrador (405,212 km2 per the Dominion of Newfoundland page) is 10.04 M km2, ratio 1.005 to the infobox. Cliopatria starts here because the Statute of Westminster (11 December 1931: 'The whole statute applied to the Dominion of Canada') made Canada self-governing; the Dominion itself is older (1867). Labrador belongs to Newfoundland until 1949.

10.03 M km2 for 1949-1972: the 1932 shape plus 1,285 cells (computed with the gazetteer) over Newfoundland and Labrador, which 'joined Canada in the final hours of 31 March 1949'. Infobox 9,984,670 km2: ratio 1.004.

correction.text: the 1976 shape, which holds the same land without the 418 lake cells

keyframe_review.note: 10.14 M km2 against 10.03 M km2 in both the 1949 and the 1976 shapes. The gazetteer shows 418 extra cells in the 1973-1975 shape, all between 50N and 67N and 125W and 96W, a belt that looks like the great lakes (Great Bear, Great Slave, Athabasca, Winnipeg and others; the match to named lakes is the researcher's reading), and none elsewhere; no border change is dated for 1973-1975 (the page's only event in the 1970s is the 13 March 1974 maritime border with Denmark, which 'skipped' Hans Island). Use the 1976 shape for these years.

10.03 M km2 for 1976-2023, the same land as 1949 (infobox 9,984,670 km2). Nunavut was cut from the Northwest Territories on 1 April 1999 and changes no outer border; the Hans Island line was defined on 19 December 2023 ('passes through Hans Island rather than skipping over it'), a land change of about one island.
Same land as 1976-2023. Nothing dated for 2024 on the pages.

region.text: the four provinces of 1867: Ontario and Quebec in their 1867 limits (the settled south, before the 1912 northward extensions), Nova Scotia and New Brunswick

ledger.note: 1 July 1867: Canadian Confederation. The British North America Act 'officially proclaimed Canadian Confederation on July 1, 1867, initially with four provinces: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick'; 'the word dominion was conferred as the country's title'. Cliopatria draws the Dominion inside the British Colonial Empire row until 1931.

ledger.note: 15 July 1870: Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory. 'The United Kingdom transferred most of its remaining land in North America to Canada' after 'Canada and the Hudson's Bay Company agreed to the terms'; 'A rectangular area ... around the city of Winnipeg was made the province of Manitoba'. The Canada page says Canada 'assumed control of Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory' (Manitoba in July 1870).
20 July 1871: British Columbia joins. 'The British colony of British Columbia joined Canada as the sixth province.'
1 July 1873: Prince Edward Island joins. 'The British colony of Prince Edward Island joined Canada as the seventh province.'

region.text: the head of Lynn Canal and the Skagway-Dyea gateway to the Yukon, the heart of the Alaska panhandle dispute

ledger.note: 1897: the Klondike rush makes the Alaska panhandle a dispute. The boundary dispute 'intensified following the 1897 Klondike Gold Rush'; the North-West Mounted Police sent a detachment to the head of Lynn Canal but 'A massive influx of American stampeders through Skagway very quickly forced the Canadian police to retreat'. The page gives no date for the police detachment.

region.text: the head of Lynn Canal and the Skagway-Dyea gateway to the Yukon, the heart of the Alaska panhandle dispute

ledger.note: 20 October 1903: the Alaska boundary is settled. 'The Alaska boundary dispute was resolved, generally in favour of the United States claim.' The Alaska page: 'Canada did not get an all-Canadian outlet from Yukon's gold fields to the Pacific Ocean'; the tribunal decision 'issued on 20 October 1903' (the Canadian judges refused to sign). Canada held none of the contested land, so there is no loss.

region.text: the island of Newfoundland and Labrador on the mainland

ledger.note: 31 March 1949: Newfoundland and Labrador join. 'Newfoundland joined Canada in the final hours of 31 March 1949'; the dominion 'included the island of Newfoundland, and Labrador on the continental mainland' (Territorial evolution page: 'joined as the tenth province'). Labrador had been awarded to Newfoundland by the Privy Council in 1927.

wars.name: Alaska boundary dispute

zones.text: the head of Lynn Canal and the Skagway-Dyea gateway to the Yukon, the heart of the Alaska panhandle dispute

wars.outcome: Tribunal award of 20 October 1903 'generally in favour of the United States claim'; Canada got no all-Canadian outlet from the Yukon to the sea.
wars.note: A diplomatic dispute, not a war; the Hay-Herbert Treaty of 1903 (day not on the page) sent it to a six-member mixed tribunal.

wars.name: Labrador boundary dispute

zones.text: Labrador, the mainland part of the Dominion of Newfoundland

wars.outcome: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council decided in Newfoundland's favour, 'against Canada'; 'Quebec has long rejected the outcome'.
wars.note: Date disagreement: 1 April 1927 (Dominion of Newfoundland page) against 11 March 1927 (Territorial evolution page). The start of the dispute is not on either page; Labrador was never in the Canada shape before 1949, so there is no contest event.

wars.name: Hans Island dispute
wars.outcome: The maritime border of 13 March 1974 'skipped' Hans Island; on 19 December 2023 the border was defined to pass through it.
wars.note: The island (about one square kilometre) is smaller than a grid cell, so no contest event is written. Machias Seal Island and North Rock with the United States, inherited in 1867 and left out of the 1984 Gulf of Maine case, likewise.

certainty.note: The inner frontiers of Rupert's Land and the Arctic are nominal and the Alaska panhandle line is disputed; the southern frontier with the United States follows treaty lines and is sharp throughout.
The Alaska line is fixed on 20 October 1903 and the Labrador boundary decided in 1927; the exceptions are the Arctic maritime limits and Hans Island, in dispute until 2023.

sources.title: Statute of Westminster 1931
sources.note: 11 December 1931: the whole statute applied to the Dominion of Canada; the British North America Acts excluded until 1982. Explains why Cliopatria starts its Canada row in 1932.

notes:
Cliopatria's Canada row begins in 1932 (after the Statute of Westminster, 11 December 1931), but the Canadian state begins on 1 July 1867: this dossier starts in 1867 and adds five new keyframes for 1867-1931, drawn as regions (Ontario and Quebec as the Upper Canada and Canada (St Lawrence) regions, the Arctic Islands as an approximate polygon). From 1867 to 1931 the same land lies inside Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row (1706-1999; by the gazetteer that row holds 98-100% of the Maritime provinces in 1867, almost all of Canada in 1900 and 1930, and in 1935 only Newfoundland and Labrador, 90%); the British dossier (eu-11) should either carry the Dominion as a vassal of the Empire (counterpart 'canada', 1867-1931) or the renderer should let this dossier win the overlap. No event is written for the Statute of Westminster because no ledger type fits a change of status.

Sanity check: infobox area 9,984,670 km2 against the shapes (9.63 M without Newfoundland and Labrador; 10.03 M with, ratio 1.005). The 1973-1975 shape (10.139 M) carries 418 extra lake cells and is adjusted to the 1976 shape. The 1949 gain of 1,285 cells is Newfoundland and Labrador.

Page budget used (5 of 5): Canada, Territorial evolution of Canada, Dominion of Newfoundland, Alaska boundary dispute, Statute of Westminster 1931. Not opened: Rupert's Land, North-West Rebellion, Canadian Confederation, Nunavut, Seshat Canada (ca_canada_dominion). Internal changes (Manitoba 1870, Keewatin 1876, Ontario's boundary 1874/1889, Yukon 1898, Alberta and Saskatchewan 1905, the 1912 extensions, Nunavut 1999) change no outer border and carry no ledger event; the Territorial evolution page dates all of them for a provincial-growth layer if wanted.

Page disagreements: Labrador decision 11 March 1927 (Territorial evolution) or 1 April 1927 (Dominion of Newfoundland).

Counterparts needing dossiers: the Hudson's Bay Company lands (Rupert's Land, group am-07-x; used here as 'hudson-s-bay-company-lands'), and the Dominion of Newfoundland (1907-1949, used as 'dominion-of-newfoundland'; Cliopatria has no Newfoundland row, am-07-x). The Colony of British Columbia and Prince Edward Island are drawn as British Colonial Empire land (the aggregate row).

Rulers: none given; the monarchy and prime ministers are not on the pages opened.

Gazetteer: 'Upper Canada' and 'Canada (St Lawrence)' are existing regions used as the 1867 Ontario and Quebec; the Arctic Islands are a polygon (the gazetteer has no Arctic Archipelago, Baffin or Ellesmere); 'Skagway' is a place with country USA.
